headline: Centre promises full support as 2 Nipah cases emerge in WB
content: The Centre on Monday assured West Bengal of full support after two suspected cases of Nipah virus disease were identified on January 11 at the Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory (VRDL) of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) at AIIMS Kalyani.Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda wrote to Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, assuring all necessary assistance from the Centre. He also spoke to the CM over the telephone and reiterated the Centre’s commitment to support the state in managing the situation.Official sources said that given the serious nature of Nipah virus infection, a zoonotic disease with high mortality and the potential for rapid spread, the situation was being handled with utmost priority.The Union Health Ministry is closely monitoring the situation in coordination with the West Bengal Government.“A National Joint Outbreak Response Team has been deployed to support the State Government in containment and public health response measures. The team comprises experts from the All India Institute of Health and Public Hygiene, Kolkata; National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune; National Institute of Epidemiology (NIE), Chennai; AIIMS Kalyani; and the Department of Wildlife, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change,” sources said.Officials said the Centre was providing comprehensive technical, logistical and operational support to the State Government. “All essential resources, including laboratory support, enhanced surveillance, case management, infection prevention and control measures, and expert guidance, have already been mobilised. The state has been advised to ensure close coordination with the deployed expert teams and to undertake meticulous contact tracing and other containment measures,” officials said.

headline: ‘Lab to land’ policy to transform farming, rural economy: Chouhan
content: Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Monday emphasised on the government’s efforts to empower small farmers through the “Lab to land” policy, saying that such an initiative will promote integrated agricultural and rural development.Addressing young leaders at the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders' Dialogue 2026, Chouhan said the policy would ensure small farmers directly benefit from technological innovations and modern farming practices.The policy aims to bridge the gap between agricultural research (lab) and actual farming practices (land) by directly connecting scientists with farmers.He urged the youth to associate themselves with the mission, contributing their skills and energy to strengthen rural development and support agricultural growth.Emphasising the crucial role of youth in driving the country’s development, the minister said their creativity and energy would be harnessed for nation building.Chouhan announced that the ministry would incorporate meaningful suggestions from youngsters into policy making, ensuring that their ideas have a direct impact on governance and development initiatives.“Through constructive ideas and teamwork, prosperity and self-reliance will reach every village,” he said.He urged youth to participate actively, assuring that their contributions would be recognised and integrated into the country’s broader vision for growth and sustainable development.Chouhan said, “Life is not meant to be wasted, but to be devoted to the attainment of a noble purpose.” He also invited talented youth to share their ideas and present their innovations.Stressing that youth were the country’s greatest asset and their empowerment was key to making India a truly developed nation, Chouhan urged them to make meaningful use of their lives, encouraging them to live not just for themselves but for society and the nation.He stressed that the awakening and participation of youth in nation building was essential for progress and prosperity.

headline: CBI grills actor-politician Vijay for 7 hours in Karur stampede case
content: The CBI on Monday questioned actor-turned-politician Vijay for close to around seven hours in connection with last year’s Karur stampede case. He is learnt to have told the agency that he was not responsible for the mishap, in which 41 persons, including nine children, were killed.The stampede in Karur, Tamil Nadu, had occurred on September 27 last year at a massive political rally addressed by Vijay, marking one of the deadliest crowd disasters in Tamil Nadu’s recent political history. The actor heads the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which he had launched in February 2024.According to sources, Vijay was questioned individually by the CBI after he arrived at the agency’s office at around 11 am. Tamil Nadu DGP S Davidson Devasirvatham was also questioned separately by the CBI.Davidson was the state’s ADGP at the time of the incident.Vijay is likely to be called for questioning again after January 15, as he is learnt to have requested the CBI to call him after Pongal (which falls on January 15).Vijay was questioned on alleged delays and crowd management lapses that took place during the rally at Karur.According to the sources, one of the key issues under scrutiny was the alleged seven-hour delay in arrival at the venue. The investigators are probing the gap between the scheduled start time of the programme and Vijay’s actual arrival. They are looking into whether the delay contributed to the crowd swelling and loss of control.The sources said Vijay’s statements would be cross-verified with police accounts.At the time of the tragedy, the Tamil Nadu Police had blamed Vijay’s alleged inordinate delay in arriving at the venue for the chaos, stating that the prolonged wait led to a surging and uncontrollable crowd.Police officials had also cited a lack of adequate food, drinking water and toilet facilities, saying the weary crowd eventually turned unruly.Vijay, however, denied the allegations, calling these a “conspiracy” by the ruling DMK, a charge the party has rejected. He countered by blaming the police for poor crowd management and for failing to clear bottlenecks on approach roads to the venue.

headline: IIT -Madras tech boosts Army artillery range by nearly 50%
content: The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras on Monday announced a defence-technology breakthrough that significantly enhances the range of artillery guns used by the Indian Army.IIT Madras said it has developed an artillery ammunition system assisted by a compact ramjet engine, extending the range of existing gun systems by nearly 50 per cent without any loss of lethality. The technology eliminates the need for new artillery platforms or costly missile systems.“Trials across multiple platforms show substantial range improvements,” IIT Madras said in a post on X.According to the institute, the range of the Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System (ATAGS) has been tested at up to 70 km from the existing 40 km. The range of the K9 Vajra gun has been extended from 36 km to 62 km, while the Dhanush artillery gun’s range has increased from 30 km to 55 km.The project, launched in 2020 in collaboration with the Army, has undergone extensive gun and field trials at Deolali and Pokhran.The project was led by Prof P A Ramakrishna of IIT Madras, along with Lt Gen P R Shankar (retd), Prof H S N Murthy, Prof G Rajesh, Prof M Ramakrishna, Prof Murugaiyan, Lt Gen Hari Mohan Iyer (retd), Prof Lazar C and Dr Yogesh Kumar Velari.

headline: PM to inaugurate Commonwealth Speakers’ conference on Jan 15; Pak, Bangladesh to skip
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth (CSPOC) on January 15. The international conference is expected to see participation from 42 of the 56 Commonwealth member nations, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla told mediapersons on Monday.The three-day conference will be held from January 14 to 16. Pakistan and Bangladesh will not participate in the summit, Birla said when asked about their presence. He, however, did not respond to a query on whether Pakistan had been invited. On Bangladesh, the Speaker said the Parliament there was currently suspended.Birla said participation at this edition would be the highest in the conference’s history, with countries including Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom attending. A total of 61 Speakers and presiding officers are expected to take part.The CSPOC will deliberate on shared parliamentary values, democratic governance and institutional cooperation.He added that a dedicated mobile application had been developed to manage conference coordination, facilitation and dissemination of information.The 27th edition of the CSPOC was hosted by Uganda in January 2024, where Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Harivansh, who led the Indian parliamentary delegation, formally assumed the role of host for the next conference.The Lok Sabha Speaker will also chair a meeting of the CSPOC Standing Committee at the Red Fort in New Delhi on Wednesday.

headline: Electronics Ministry refutes reports on smartphone source code demand
content: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has firmly denied media reports suggesting that the government plans to force smartphone makers to share source code and implement multiple software changes as part of security measures, a move that reportedly drew opposition from tech giants like Apple and Samsung.In a statement, MeitY said: “These news reports have not quoted any statement from smartphone manufacturers or industry associations representing them. Instead, they have selectively ignored comments from industry associations, clearly indicating a mischievous intent to sensationalise the news.”The ministry clarified that the government was taking continuous steps to ensure user safety and protect personal data in the rapidly evolving digital ecosystem. Authorities reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cybersecurity and safeguarding citizens’ privacy.With over a billion mobile users in India, smartphones have become central to financial transactions, delivery of public services, and storage of sensitive personal information. This widespread usage makes mobile devices a prime target for cybercriminals, the statement noted.Any compromise of mobile security can lead to identity theft, financial losses, privacy violations and unauthorised access to sensitive information such as banking details, photographs and login credentials. Businesses are also at risk, as unsecured devices can result in data breaches and operational disruptions. The government is actively working to implement robust security measures and raise user awareness to mitigate these risks, ensuring a safer digital environment for individuals and organisations alike.MeitY said it routinely conducted consultations on aspects such as safety compliance, electromagnetic interference and compatibility (EMI/EMC) parameters, Indian language support, interface requirements and security standards. Following stakeholder consultations, detailed discussions are held with industry on various dimensions of security requirements.Emphasising its commitment to working closely with industry stakeholders and addressing concerns constructively, the ministry said, “MeitY has been engaging with industry representatives to better understand technical challenges, compliance burdens and international best practices adopted by smartphone manufacturers.”The ministry reiterated that all legitimate concerns raised by the industry would be examined with an open mind in the best interests of both the country and the industry.
